newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia Nov company debts rise to HRK7.8 bln - paper.
newsitem.headline: Croatia Nov company debts rise to HRK7.8 bln - paper.

text.p: Croatian intercompany debts increased 0.5 billion kuna ($85.4 million) to 7.8 billion kuna in November last year from October, daily Vjesnik reported on Wednesday.
November's total was more than double the amount of money available in the system at the end of that month, Vjesnik said quoting preliminary figures of the state payments bureau (ZAP).
Though used as an insolvency indicator, intercompany debts are not a true gauge since they do not include all overdue payments such as tax and loan interest.
ZAP executes money orders from companies' giro accounts that are kept by commercial banks and can block these accounts in case of insolvency.
It reported 16,830 businesses, or some 80 percent of all registered companies and private entrepreneurs, had their accounts blocked for 60 days last year, Vjesnik said.
Some 5.5 percent more firms defaulted on payments to other firms in November than a month earlier. Almost one-third of all debts were accumulated in the trade sector.
Debtors were mostly private businesses with roughly 47,500 employees. They ran up almost 4.6 billion kuna debt to other companies through November.
State-owned firms, employeeing 37,400 people, owed just over a billion kuna.
Mixed companies and cooperatives with a total workforce of 62,200 accounted for the remainder of the debt.
